Refined assessment with SLOOS overlay

- Positive drivers (reinforced by SLOOS): Labor-market momentum remains strong and policy is still accommodative in rate terms. Importantly, SLOOS points to broad easing in bank lending standards across residential real estate, multifamily, nonfarm nonresidential CRE, consumer credit (credit cards, auto, HELOCs, jumbo/QM/non-QM), plus increased credit limits and lower auto loan rates. Banks expect stronger demand in credit cards and C&I, and foreign banks report stronger CRE loan demand alongside eased CRE standards. This indicates a supportive credit supply backdrop that should buttress household and business spending as QE is tapered.

- Offsetting factors: Inflation is above target and the Committee is accelerating tapering, signaling eventual rate hikes and some tightening via firmer long-end yields. SLOOS also notes pockets of softer current demand in C&I and auto, tempering the breadth of strength. Financial stability vulnerabilities (elevated valuations, business leverage, fund and market-structure fragilities, and duration risk) mean policy normalization could transmit more forcefully than the statement alone implies.

- Market implications: With taper reducing downward pressure on term premia, yields can drift higher, but easier bank credit standards and improving expected loan demand should cushion overall financial conditions versus a pure-taper read.

Bottom line: Still mildly positive on growth and employment, and more constructive than the base case once SLOOS easing in credit standards and expected demand are factored in; risks from inflation, normalization, and FSR vulnerabilities keep the tone tempered rather than outright bullish.
